newsitem.title: USA: Sorry, we sell software, not pornography.
newsitem.headline: Sorry, we sell software, not pornography.

text.p: Exasperated by a barrage of requests for services it does not provide, a computer software company is changing its name -- X Inside -- in the hopes of clearing up the confusion that it distributes pornography.
The developer of computer graphics software said Wednesday it is changing its name to Xi Graphics in order to attract the kind of customer it serves best.
"We develop software," said Richard Van Dyke, the Denver-based company's marketing vice president. "We do not address the performance issues of the sexually adventurous."
The company's original name brought a barrage of requests for pornographic material, he said.
"An aspiring model even went so far as to show me a portfolio of highly suggestive photographs," said Thomas Roell, president and chief technology designer. "We felt a name change was in order."
Van Dyke said he was confident the name change would clear things up.

"We believe the new name will effectively relieve us of some of the wacky calls we've been getting," he said. "And by adding 'graphics' to our name ... we are better representing our company's mission to provide graphics software solutions."
